## Intravector Sums

Suppose we wanted the sums of the *entries* of a vector; we call this the **intra-vector sum** to differentiate from the "inter-vector sum" of summing vectors, which is already supplied as a basic move. A naive approach would be to repeatedly use cycle to obtain encryptions of $$(z_1, \ldots, z_{N/2}), (z_2, \ldots, z_{N/2}, z_1), \ldots, (z_{N/2}, z_1, \ldots, z_{N/2-1})$$ and then add them as in the inter-vector case. This puts the sum in every coordinate.

However, we can make this faster by noticing the following. Suppose we cycled by $1$ and added instead, then we would be able to get: $$\mathtt{enc}(z_1 + z_2, z_2 + z_3, z_3 + z_4, \cdots)$$ then cycling by $2$ and adding to itself would put $z_1 + z_2 + z_3 + z_4$ in the first position, but with only 2 additions instead of $3$. Extending this method, we can sum all the numbers with $\log({N/2})$ operations.


@fig-intravector-sums shows the reduction tree for 8 slots: each row adds a copy of the row above cycled by 1, 2 and then 4, and because the cycles wrap around, every slot ends with the full sum, not just the first.

```{r}
#| label: fig-intravector-sums
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| fig-cap: "Summing eight slots with three cycle-and-adds, shifting by 1, 2, then 4, forms a binary tree."
#| fig-alt: "Four rows of eight boxes. The top row holds z1 through z8. After cycling by 1 and adding, each box holds a sum of two neighbors, such as z1 + z2; after cycling by 2, a sum of four, such as z1 + ... + z4; after cycling by 4, every box holds the sum of all 8, with indices wrapping from 8 back to 1. Orange boxes mark the entries that reach slot 1, and arrows run from the two inputs of each orange box into it, forming a binary tree."

library(ggplot2)

slots <- 8
shifts <- c(1, 2, 4)

# Simulate: each row holds, per slot, the set of input indices it sums.
# Shifting by s gives slot j the old content of slot j + s (wrapping), then add.
rows <- list(as.list(1:slots))
for (s in shifts) {
  prev <- rows[[length(rows)]]
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- lapply(1:slots, function(j) {
    src <- (j - 1 + s) %% slots + 1
    sort(union(prev[[j]], prev[[src]]))
  })
}

# Name a set of indices as a cyclic range, e.g. {7, 8, 1, 2} -> "7-2".
# Plotmath label for the sum a cell holds, e.g. z[7] + cdots + z[2] (wrapping mod 8).
# Hot cells are bold.
range_label <- function(idx, slot, hot) {
  n <- length(idx)
  last <- (slot + n - 2) %% slots + 1
  lab <- if (n == 1) paste0("z[", slot, "]")
         else if (n == 2) paste0("z[", slot, "] + z[", last, "]")
         else if (n < slots) paste0("z[", slot, "] + cdots + z[", last, "]")
         else "\"all 8\""
  if (hot) paste0("bold(", lab, ")") else lab
}

# Which cells of each row feed slot 1 of the last row (work backwards).
need <- vector("list", length(rows))
need[[length(rows)]] <- 1
for (r in length(shifts):1) {
  need[[r]] <- sort(unique(c(need[[r + 1]], (need[[r + 1]] - 1 + shifts[r]) %% slots + 1)))
}

cells <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(rows), function(r) {
  data.frame(
    row = r - 1, slot = 1:slots,
    hot = 1:slots %in% need[[r]],
    label = vapply(1:slots, function(j) range_label(rows[[r]][[j]], j, j %in% need[[r]]), "")
  )
}))

neutral <- "grey50"
orange <- "#E69F00"

row_names <- c("Input", paste0("Cycle by ", shifts, ", add"))
steps <- data.frame(row = 0:3, label = row_names)

# Every partial sum (orange cell) gets an arrow from both of its inputs: the
# same slot one row up, and the slot `shift` to the right. Arrows land on the
# left and right of the top edge, so the two heads never overlap.
rg <- 2      # vertical distance between rows
th <- 0.7    # tile height
feeds <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(shifts), function(r) {
  tg <- need[[r + 1]]
  data.frame(
    x = c(tg, tg + shifts[r]),
    xend = c(tg - 0.2, tg + 0.2),
    row = r - 1
  )
}))

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(
    data = cells,
    aes(x = slot, y = row * rg, fill = hot),
    width = 0.92, height = th, color = neutral, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = cells,
    aes(x = slot, y = row * rg, label = label),
    parse = TRUE, color = ifelse(cells$hot, "black", neutral), size = 3.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = steps,
    aes(x = 0.35, y = row * rg, label = label),
    color = neutral, size = 5, fontface = "bold", hjust = 1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = feeds,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = row * rg + th / 2 + 0.05, yend = (row + 1) * rg - th / 2 - 0.05),
    color = orange, linewidth = 0.9,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = orange, `FALSE` = NA), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-2.4, slots + 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )
```

The savings grow quickly with the number of slots (@fig-cycle-cost). For $N = 2^{16}$ the full vector has $N/2 = 2^{15}$ slots, and the sum takes 15 cycles instead of 32,767.

```{r}
#| label: fig-cycle-cost
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| fig-cap: "Cycles needed to sum $n$ slots one at a time versus by cycle-and-add."
#| fig-alt: "Log-log plot of cycles needed against the number of slots, from 2 to 2^15. Summing one at a time, a solid grey line, grows to 32,767 cycles; cycle-and-add, a dashed orange line, grows only to 15."
library(ggplot2)

orange <- "#E69F00"
k <- 1:15                                 # n = 2^k slots, up to N/2 = 2^15
cost <- rbind(
  data.frame(n = 2^k, cycles = 2^k - 1, method = "one at a time"),
  data.frame(n = 2^k, cycles = k,       method = "cycle-and-add")
)
pow2 <- function(b) parse(text = paste0("2^", log2(b)))

ggplot(cost, aes(n, cycles, colour = method, linetype = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = 2^9, y = 2^11, label = "'one at a time: '*n - 1", parse = TRUE,
           colour = "grey50", size = 5, fontface = "bold", hjust = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 2^9, y = 2^5, label = "'cycle-and-add: '*log[2]~n", parse = TRUE,
           colour = orange, size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 2^15, y = 32767, label = "32767",
           colour = "grey50", size = 4, hjust = 1.2, vjust = -0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 2^15, y = 15, label = "15",
           colour = orange, size = 4, hjust = 1.2, vjust = -0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("one at a time" = "grey50", "cycle-and-add" = orange), guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("one at a time" = "solid", "cycle-and-add" = "dashed"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = 2^seq(1, 15, by = 2), labels = pow2) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = 2^seq(0, 15, by = 3), labels = pow2,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "number of slots n", y = "cycles needed") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.15),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "grey50"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "grey50")
  )
```

Here are a couple of general consequences of being able to sum: 

1. **dot product**: given encrypted vectors of $c_*$ and $d_*$, we can multiply to get $\mathtt{enc}(c_1d_1, c_2d_2, \ldots)$, and then sum to get the dot product. 

2. **(complex) inner product**: since we can take the conjugate of $d_*$, we can compute the complex inner product $$c_1\overline{d_1} + \cdots + c_{N/2}\overline{d_{N/2}}.$$
